prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted frail elderly animal tamer: white gray slicked-back hair, large dark glasses, long thin face and neck, dark teal cardigan, ochre vest, cream shirt, slim brown trousers, waist pouch. Body ~41 native pixels tall. Preserve his face and thin silhouette. No cigarette.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 4 columns x 2 rows. Top row four alternating walking phases, gentle elderly posture, near leg forward, far passing, far leg forward, near passing. Bottom row (4) startled hit recoil with hand shielding chest alive, (5) recover, (6) walking with one hand extended BACK toward a following animal (do not draw an animal), (7) same beckoning lead pose with opposite leg forward. All facing RIGHT. No spell or magic.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
